Introduction

What is Reiki? In Japanese, the character Rei has many meanings, but the most common are universe, God, and the Absolute. A concept close to Rei, more familiar from Eastern culture and philosophy, is Tao, signifying divine light, a higher law, order, or a kind of ideal standard.
The character Ki means vital energy, life force, the very breath of Life.
Thus, Reiki is most often translated as universal life energy.

The idea is very simple: the whole universe is permeated with Reiki energy, which can be used in simple methods of working with problems of body and soul. The source describes the method as entirely safe: it claims that the body receives exactly as much healing energy as it needs and directs it to the area where it is most needed.

Unlike psychic healing, which is said to require the healer to develop special extrasensory abilities, the source teaches that anyone can use Reiki energy. A person initiated into the Reiki system acts as a channel for this life energy and, according to the tradition, does not expend their own strength; instead, they are said to be strengthened and enriched by it.

Reiki is also presented as one of the oldest forms of healing by laying on hands. According to the account given here, it was known for thousands of years among different peoples. Its practitioners were often venerated as holy embodiments of God. Such holy elders were known in Japan and China, and in Russia they were regarded as saints. The tradition was later almost forgotten, with a revival beginning in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.

The source states that Mikao Usui rediscovered this ancient system of Reiki healing in 1922 and named it Usui Reiki Ryoho Gakkai, the Usui Society for the Reiki Healing Method. It says that the society still exists in Japan. At first the school admitted only Japanese students, but later the teaching spread throughout the world. In this telling, it was regarded as a freely received teaching rather than a system owned by a particular author, revealed to Mikao Usui during long meditations at temples on the sacred Mount Kurama. Today, it says, thousands practice Reiki worldwide and millions believe that Reiki helped them recover from illness.

By naming his teaching Usui Reiki Ryoho, Mikao Usui indicated that he was working with the particular aspect of Reiki energy that had been revealed to him. According to the tradition, the teaching passes from Master to student through an initiation: each Reiki Master, originally Usui himself, opens the student's channel and transmits the capacity to work with Reiki energy.
Upon reaching a certain level, a Reiki Master may modify the system in keeping with their own worldview, developing their own methods and skills for working with
the system. The result may be an entirely new practice with its own distinctive energetic qualities.

Thus, after Mikao Usui's death, one of his students, who was a physician, added more medical aspects and modified the Reiki system. This student was Chujiro Hayashi. According to the source, he founded a clinic in the United States, established a society of Reiki followers called Usui Shiho Ryoho, and developed hand positions suited to clinical work, where several healers often worked with the same patient at once.

Today, besides Usui Reiki Ryoho, there are many other practices that draw on Reiki energy. All were created by Reiki Masters. Well-known examples include Tantra Reiki, Kundalini Reiki, and Reiki Yggdrasil. The Reiki Yggdrasil system was introduced to the world by Nikolai Zhuravlev, described here as having practiced methods of exploring and transforming oneself and one's surroundings for more than twenty years.
Why did Nikolai Zhuravlev link Reiki with the concept of Yggdrasil in his distinctive system?

Yggdrasil is the World Tree of Germanic and Norse mythology: an enormous evergreen ash (or yew) steeped in sacred mead, connecting nine worlds, with the destinies of people inscribed upon its leaves. The ancient Scandinavians imagined the whole of existence in the form of this tree.

Yggdrasil is a classic axis mundi, the axis of the world connecting heaven and earth or the underworld, the world of human beings and the world of the gods. This world axis is a cosmic bridge or road between all the worlds.

Yggdrasil literally means the steed or horse of Yggr, one of Odin's names, meaning the Terrible One. The name also alludes to Odin hanging for nine days and nights, pierced by a spear upon the ash tree, to obtain sacred knowledge (in the North, the gallows could be called the 'horse of the hanged'), and to the possibility of traveling from one world to another by means of the Tree. The council of the gods gathered daily beneath the sacred Tree. Its three roots extended into three worlds: Midgard, the world of humans; Jotunheim, the world of frost giants; and Niflheim, the world of the dead and of mist. Three springs rose beside its roots: the spring of fate, the spring of wisdom, and the source of all earthly rivers. Odin gave up his right eye for a drink from the spring and gained inexhaustible wisdom. On the bark of Yggdrasil, Odin revealed the runes to the world in his own blood.

The word runes is connected with the old Germanic root ru or Gothic runa, translated as 'secret' or 'mysterious whisper.' In the ancient world runes were used not only for writing but also for mystical rituals and divination. The tradition holds that people still turn to the mysterious magic of the old runes in pursuit of power, knowledge, and health.

The concept of Rei may likewise be imagined as a Tree, with all that exists forming its branches and the energy of Ki as the life-giving sap nourishing the whole tree from roots to leaves. Rei also symbolizes the human spirit, wisdom, and the ability to become aware and develop. This aspect of the person is regarded as immortal. Ki represents strength, health, and vital potential.

According to this teaching, Reiki helps people harmonize their inner dimensions, soul and body, and their relationships with the world and those around them. What could be more harmonious than a tree—especially the World Tree?

Legend tells that the first human couple came to life from two tree trunks found on a shore. The first man was made from an ash branch and named Ask, meaning 'ash.' The first woman was Embla, a name interpreted here as 'willow' (or, according to other sources, 'alder' or 'elm'). The idea that humans descend from trees was widespread in ancient Europe.

The Tree of Life is the universe in which God dwells. Human beings are themselves miniature Trees of Life and, by reconnecting with the Tree, regain their lost immortality. All negative actions, manifestations, and emotions are said to separate a person from that once-perfect state. The flow of Reiki energy through Yggdrasil is understood as bringing the person back to God. By channeling the energy of the runes, the person makes life more conscious, gains mastery over what happens, and develops more rapidly.

By combining and reworking two ancient teachings—Reiki's life-giving energy and the power of the Scandinavian Tree Yggdrasil—Nikolai Zhuravlev created his own distinctive system of understanding the world, which he called Reiki Yggdrasil.

By attuning to the general flow of the runes, the practitioner is said to gradually feel energy filling body and consciousness, creating a favorable state for self-realization in modern society and the ability to change the surrounding world for the better. The Reiki Yggdrasil system addresses many aspects of life: health, relationships, work, money, experiences and knowledge attributed to past lives, and much more.

Despite its depth, the Reiki Yggdrasil system is presented as accessible to everyone. In the source's metaphor, not only the god Odin but an ordinary person may drink the wisdom of Mimir's spring. The system is described as simple to understand and possible to learn with modest effort.

By gradually becoming aware of the power of Reiki energy (hereafter simply 'the Flow') and understanding the structure of Yggdrasil as the structure of the universe's cosmic consciousness (so that the Flow is part of that structure, while the Tree is itself part of the Flow), the practitioner can ascend, as if on a ladder, through the levels of Reiki Yggdrasil.

The levels of Reiki Yggdrasil. The system includes five basic levels of initiation. After completing all five, the student receives the rank of Reiki Yggdrasil Master. Each level consists of different attunements. An attunement is a particular quality of the Flow, its special frequency. The task is to learn to distinguish these attunements within the general Flow and activate them when needed. The source describes the course as building a powerful framework that projects the Yggdrasil Tree into the body and consciousness, making the practitioner more stable and successful.
The first level includes the following attunements:
• Healing
• Intuition
• Protection
• Working with a Situation

At the first level, you learn skills intended to address common difficulties and thereby improve the quality of your own life and the lives of others. These include practices described as healing and self-healing, the cultivation of intuition, and the ability to protect yourself and others from hostile outside influences.
The second level includes the following attunements:
• Charging an Object
• Activating the Money Flow
• Cleansing People; Cleansing a Room
• Breaking a Connection

At the second level, you learn the practice of charging objects and symbolically cleansing yourself, others, objects, and surrounding space of negative structures. This level also addresses building a healthier relationship with money through the 'money flow' attunement.
The third level includes eight attunements:
• Life Purpose
• Emotion
• Activation
• Power
• Sexuality
• Flight
• Intellect
• Karma

According to the course, the third level helps you recognize your true path and goal in life. It discusses clearing negative information attributed to past incarnations and karmic blocks and finding harmony in your emotional life. It also speaks of becoming more attractive to the opposite sex.
Leadership qualities are activated. The Flight attunement is said to allow consciousness to shift through space and time.
The fourth level includes the following attunements:
• Vision
• Past Lives
• Creating a Situation
• Knowledge
The fourth level is described as activating the third eye (Ajna) and cultivating clairvoyant perception and the ability to create desired situations.
The fifth-level attunements are:
• Connection with the World
• Connection with the Gods

The fifth level is intended to expand consciousness, unite conscious and subconscious awareness, and work with situations on a global level, as well as draw upon the symbolic qualities of the Norse gods.
